scenes: They used a nuclear weapons supercomputer, to mine bitcoin.
Sah-rov, Russia. A closed city that doesn't appear on maps.
This is where the Soviet Union built its first atomic bomb. Today, it still works on nuclear warheads.
Inside: a supercomputer with one petaflop of power. A million billion calculations every second.
February twenty eighteen. Bitcoin had touched almost twenty thousand dollars two months earlier.
And a few engineers get an idea. They quietly put the supercomputer to work mining bitcoin.
One problem. Mining needs the internet. And a nuclear weapons lab is supposed to stay offline.
The moment they connect it, security sees everything. Russia's security service, the F S B, walks in.
The lab calls it 'a hopeless and criminal offense.'
The price? One engineer was fined four hundred fifty thousand rubles. About seven thousand dollars.
The most powerful computer in town, and all it earned them was a fine.
Side money on a work computer is never secret. Someone is always watching. Follow Chain Secrets.
